# Services — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

Listings here are services, not physical items. Photos that are logos, posters, or before/after shots are normal and not suspicious by themselves. This space is scam-prone in Nepal (fake recruitment, advance-fee fraud, especially overseas manpower), so caution is the default: publish only when the posting is unusually clearly legitimate — a named provider, a concrete service, a real location or contact context.

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Servicing & Repair: typically around 1,250, most listings 500–2,800 (6 listings)
- Professional Services: typically around 2,000, most listings 200–10,000 (6 listings)
- Body Massage: typically around 1,200, most listings 400–6,800 (4 listings)
- IT Services: typically around 600, most listings 300–2,300 (4 listings)
- Tours & Travels: typically around 30,000, most listings 15,000–230,000 (3 listings)

Every subcategory has fewer than 10 listings — data is thin, lean on general judgment. Service prices are quotes or starting rates, so wide spread is normal and price alone rarely decides a verdict. Exception: a Tours & Travels package priced far below any plausible cost (e.g., an international trip for a few thousand NPR) is an advance-fee scam signal → hold. (Beauty Services omitted: 4 listings with an outlier-distorted p90.)

## What good listings look like
- "Wall mount TV Installation Services in KTM Nepal" — Rs 1,000
- "furniture and office chiar repair" — Rs 1,500

A good listing names the specific service offered, the service area/city, and a rate or starting price; the description identifies who provides it (shop, workshop, or technician). Note: most recent samples in this category were actually physical goods posted in the wrong place — a title like these two, describing work performed, is the expected shape.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Overseas employment / manpower / "work abroad" or visa-guarantee postings: hold unless it names a verifiable licensed recruitment agency — advance-fee recruitment fraud is the dominant scam pattern in Nepal.
- Any service demanding upfront "registration", "processing", or "booking" fees before anything is delivered, or promising guaranteed loans, visas, or lottery/immigration outcomes.
- Obvious physical goods posted as Services are frequent here (real examples: "iPhone 8+", "iPhone xr 64gb", "Redmi note 14", "ns200" motorbike, "headphone new box", therapy oils/supplements) — hold wrong-category items for recategorization.
- Massage/spa listings whose wording or photos suggest personal companionship rather than a legitimate therapy or salon business.
